method sort_array(array: seq<int>) returns (result: seq<int>)
    requires array != null
    ensures |result| == |array| // The result has the same length as the input array
    ensures forall i :: 0 <= i < |result| ==> result[i] in array // The result contains only elements from the input array
    ensures (array.Length == 0 ==> result == []) // If the input is an empty array, the output is also an empty array
    ensures (array.Length == 1 ==> result == array) // If the input has one element, the output is the same element
    ensures (sum(array[0], array[array.Length - 1]) % 2 == 0 ==> 
             isSorted(result, false)) // If sum is even, result is sorted in descending order
    ensures (sum(array[0], array[array.Length - 1]) % 2 == 1 ==> 
             isSorted(result, true)) // If sum is odd, result is sorted in ascending order

method isSorted(arr: seq<int>, ascending: bool) returns (res: bool)
    requires arr != null
    ensures res == (forall i, j :: 0 <= i < j < |arr| ==> 
                    (ascending ==> arr[i] <= arr[j]) && 
                    (!ascending ==> arr[i] >= arr[j]))

problem_data.prompt:
def sort_array(array):
    """
    Given an array of non-negative integers, return a copy of the given array after sorting,
    you will sort the given array in ascending order if the sum( first index value, last index value) is odd,
    or sort it in descending order if the sum( first index value, last index value) is even.

    Note:
    * don't change the given array.

    Examples:
    * sort_array([]) => []
    * sort_array([5]) => [5]
    * sort_array([2, 4, 3, 0, 1, 5]) => [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
    * sort_array([2, 4, 3, 0, 1, 5, 6]) => [6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0]
    """
problem_data.canonical_solution: return [] if len(array) == 0 else sorted(array, reverse= (array[0]+array[-1]) % 2 == 0)
